gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-benga: Wire-bent s curves that never thin at the spine give Existence its industrial stamp. And Noto Serif Bengali brings restrained thick-and-thin strokes with fine hairlines, so the heading grabs the eye while the serif settles into the reading.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-devan: Existence runs one unmodulated line through every glyph, which gives its wide portholes a stark, machined look. Noto Serif Devanagari softens that with medium stroke contrast.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-dives: Noto Serif Dives Akuru has short capitals among tall small letters. Its soft, hand-inked modulation makes a warm foil for Existence, which offers no calligraphic shading at all and stays rigidly mechanical.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-dogra: Strokes that look cut from wire, with terminals stopping well short of the bowl, make Existence unmistakable. Noto Serif Dogra answers with a faint crayon-like rhythm.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-ethio: A plain stripe of constant ink, with counters like wide glass portholes, defines Existence at a glance. Noto Serif Ethiopic brings moderate thick-thin transitions, so its words read as solid blocks.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-georg: Noto Serif Georgian has lowercase swollen like tightly coiled rope, with a subdued contrast and a slight pinch where curves meet stems. Existence is the plain, unshaded line that never swells, strongest as a heading, while the classic serif handles the reading.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-grant: Hard-edged and industrial, Existence gives its crossbars the same heft as its stems. Noto Serif Grantha, a text serif with thinner hairlines and oversized small letters, tempers it.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-gujar: Industrial wire, bent into letters. Existence keeps every stroke constant, and Noto Serif Gujarati, a classic serif with soft contrast, would sit comfortably beneath it at an ordinary reading size.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-gurmu: Existence has no thick-thin pulse, just constant lines and wide glass portholes that earn their keep big and short. Noto Serif Gurmukhi, a classic serif with a generous x-height, shifts weight gradually, like thread against yarn.
